And he promised that if it were given to him,
he would release a multitude of Arab captives who were with him.
Then al-Muttaqi assembled the scribes of their faith and asked
whether the Law permitted giving such a relic to the Christians,
or not.
And they answered:
"Although it is more fitting for us to be blessed by this Mandylion,
yet for the sake of the Muslims who are distressed, hungry, and naked, it is right to give [it] to them."
At this time,
when a certain general named Tuzun grew powerful in Baghdad,
King al-Muttaqi was afraid of him,
and he took his women and his servants
and went up to Callinicus,
and he stayed there for some time.
Then this Tuzun sent to him and reproached him,
[saying,] "Why did he withdraw from his throne?" And he swore to him and so coaxed him.
And he arose and went down to Baghdad.
And when this Tuzun heard that he had arrived by water,
he assembled his forces and went out to meet the king.
And he dismounted and kissed the ground,
and walked on foot before him.
And the king urged him and made him mount.
Then this Tuzun,
while treachery was lurking in his heart,
signaled to his companions,
and they surrounded the king and those who were his.
And before he entered the palace,
they drew swords against him to kill him,
unless he abdicated.
And when he was constrained,
he abdicated and bore witness against himself.
They brought him into the palace and imprisoned him,
and they brought Abdallah, the son of al-Muktafi, and made him king,
and they gave him the surname al-Mustakfi.
These things [happened] in the year 333,
333 of the Arabs.
After al-Muttaqi, al-Mustakfi, the son of al-Muktafi, [reigned] one year and four months.
And in the very year that he became king,
various nations went forth: Alans, Slavs, and Lezgins,
and they reached as far as Azerbaijan.
And they conquered the city named Bardha'a,
and they killed in it about twenty thousand human beings (souls), and departed.
And against King al-Mustakfi, the nobles again plotted treachery.
And on one of the days, as he was sitting upon his throne,
the nobles entered as was customary,
and kissed the ground before him, and kissed his hand, and stood.
And when their number was complete,
one of them, the one who entered last,
kissed the ground
and approached the king.
And as he supposed that he was approaching to kiss his hand,
he extended his hand to him.
